lesson.title: Serve. Then See.
lesson.hook: Two connected decisions. Prepare, read the ball, choose.
lesson.liveIntro: Your wide serve is on its way. The returner has not struck it yet.

sv1A.name: What does this return offer?
sv1A.sit: The return lands short. You have time to move in and organise.
opts: Controlled pressure into the open side
Depth through the middle with margin

lines.A: You step into the short reply and use the opening. Keep playing.
lines.B: Depth through the middle is sound. You also had room to apply pressure.

sv1A.take: The serve starts the pattern. The return decides your next shot.
sv1A.payoff: The serve starts the pattern. The return decides your next shot.
sv1A.principle: Recover after the serve. Read the return before attacking.
sv1A.why: Recover after the serve so you can respond to the return you see. A short reply and organised contact can offer controlled pressure. Guessing before the return adds a correction if the ball arrives elsewhere. A deep middle reply remains a sound option.

sv1B.name: What does this return offer?
sv1B.sit: The return lands short. Your early guess leaves you adjusting again.
opts: Controlled pressure into the open side
Depth through the middle with margin

lines.A: It lands here, but you force a direction change while adjusting.
lines.B: You choose a larger target while adjusting. The point continues.

sv1B.take: The serve starts the pattern. The return decides your next shot.
sv1B.payoff: The serve starts the pattern. The return decides your next shot.
sv1B.principle: Recover after the serve. Read the return before attacking.
sv1B.why: Recover after the serve so you can respond to the return you see. A short reply and organised contact can offer controlled pressure. Guessing before the return adds a correction if the ball arrives elsewhere. A deep middle reply remains a sound option.

sv1.name: Where do you get ready for the return?
sv1.sit: Your wide serve is on its way. The returner has not struck it yet.
sv1.q: Where do you get ready for the return?
opts: Recover balanced; keep both wings available
Commit to the forehand before they hit

lines.A: You recover to read either wing. Now watch the actual return.
lines.B: You commit before their hit. The return still has to be read.

summaries.10: You recovered. Let the actual return guide the next shot.
summaries.11: You recovered, read the short return and chose from an organised contact.
summaries.01: You corrected the early guess and chose a larger target.
summaries.00: You guessed early, then pressed the angle while still adjusting.

pro.label: Coach’s lens · Prepare, then decide
pro.moment: LTA coach Matt Smith describes closing distance with larger steps, making smaller adjustments near contact, and recovering after a shot.
pro.read: Our application: recover after the serve with room to respond. Read the actual return before deciding how much pressure it permits.
pro.src: LTA · Improve your tennis footwork · Matt Smith

drill.name: Prepare, then call it
drill.how: Have a partner alternate shorter and deeper returns. Recover after serving, then say “pressure” or “margin” from the return you see. Keep the rally going.
